chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥajjāl, from Thaʿlabah ibn Maymūn, from ʿImrān ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: When does the night prayer become due? He said: When the twilight disappears, and the twilight is the redness. Then ʿUbayd Allāh said: May Allah set you aright, after the redness disappears, an intense broad light still remains. So Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: Twilight is only the redness, and the light is not part of the twilight.

key_terms.الشَّفَقُ: the twilight that marks the beginning of ʿishāʾ time
key_terms.الْحُمْرَةُ: the red glow in the sky after sunset, identified here as twilight
key_terms.الْعَتَمَةُ: the night prayer, meaning ʿishāʾ in this context
key_terms.ضَوْءٌ: the remaining light in the sky that is distinguished from twilight
key_terms.مُعْتَرِضٌ: spread across the horizon; describing the lingering broad light

ai.seo_question: When does the time for ʿishāʾ begin according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the beginning time of the ʿishāʾ prayer by defining الشَّفَق as the red twilight. It clarifies that the remaining bright lateral light in the sky after the redness vanishes does not count as الشَّفَق, and therefore does not delay the obligation time.
